capabilities: Import timestamped transcripts from video, podcast, and local media
Play media with synced transcript highlighting and segment controls
Translate segments and generate study cards with AI providers
Look up words offline and build a vocabulary book
Practice dictation, shadowing, and spaced review
extras: Desktop-only; mobile support is experimental. Public YouTube caption import uses an unofficial interface, and Bilibili/YouTube public interfaces may change. AI translation and chat require provider API keys and may incur charges; the interface and translation target are Simplified Chinese.
problem: Obsidian lacks a built-in way to turn video and podcast transcripts into timestamped language-study material with playback, lookup, and review.

relations.evidence: Embedded YouTube player using the privacy-enhanced youtube-nocookie.com domain
Local cached Bilibili playback with an optional cache folder outside the vault
paste a Spotify show or episode link in the import dialog or RSS sidebar to use its public podcast feed
Paste a Spotify or Apple Podcasts show or episode link to import a public podcast through its RSS feed
use Baidu Translate, DeepSeek, Kimi, or an OpenAI-compatible service in a draggable floating card
Local Whisper Base English transcription when a video is spoken in English but has no English subtitle track
Automatic local yt-dlp fallback on desktop when it is already installed
The compressed exam-and-frequency subset of ECDICT remains inside main.js
keep Hugging Face as the default or enter a trusted compatible HTTPS source

summary: Language-study workspace that imports timestamped YouTube, Bilibili, podcast, and local-video transcripts for playback, translation, dictation, and vocabulary review.
